title: Quantile-driven elastic trancheer to reduce prefill padding and improve kernel affinity
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: Current microbatch shaping buckets requests by coarse fixed-length boundaries which causes excess prefill padding and suboptimal kernel utilization for mixed workloads (short interactive prompts + occasional long system messages). On high QPS routes we see up to 40% padded tokens per-request on median and long-tail padding driving GPU memory churn and reduced throughput.

Goal: Implement a quantile-driven elastic bucketing ("trancheer") with online histogram estimation and kernel-affinity hints that: (1) reduces padded tokens per request by >=30% on representative workloads; (2) preserves P95 latency SLOs for prefill and decode; (3) keeps scheduling overhead <5% of current runtime CPU time; and (4) surfaces clear observability for rollout and rollback.

Approach:
- Online distribution estimation: maintain lightweight per-route quantile sketches (t-digest) of requested sequence lengths (prefill + decode horizon) with exponential decay so the estimator adapts to changing traffic.
- Elastic tranches: instead of fixed-width buckets, compute tranche boundaries at configurable quantiles (e.g., p10, p30, p60, p85, p95) and dynamically merge/split tranches when the local variance falls below/above thresholds.
- Pad reduction strategy: when building a microbatch, use tranche-aware packing to co-locate similar-length requests; within tranche prefer slotting that minimizes max pad per-GPU. For the highest-density tranche we enable micro-interleaving with shared KV caches to allow tighter packing without hurting decode latency.
- Kernel affinity hints: annotate tranche metadata with recommended kernel selection parameters (e.g., fused-attention flag, block-size choice, quantization level). The scheduler will preferentially route tranches to compatible worker pools or select compatible kernel variants during prefill.
- Prefill-aware prioritization: implement soft-prioritization for prefill-heavy requests so that prefill scheduling cooperates with decode-phase batching to avoid double-padding across stages.
- Safety & fallback: if the online estimator confidence is low or tranche load is unstable, fall back to the current fixed bucketing algorithm; add cooldown windows to avoid oscillation.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Frequent tranche recomputation increases scheduler overhead vs. stale tranche boundaries causing extra padding. We settle on a hybrid: fast lightweight adjustments every epoch (1s) and full recompute every 30s or when a tranche crosses a stability threshold.
- Aggressive packing can increase tail latency for some requests; we will cap maximum coalescing window per-request and expose a route-level "latency budget" flag that app teams can set.

Success metrics:
- Mean padded tokens per request decreased by >=30% on canary routes.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) increase >=12% on mixed-length workloads.
- Prefill P95 latency regression <5% relative to baseline SLO.
- Scheduler CPU increase <5% of current runtime overhead.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype: implement offline trancheer library and simulator to replay traces and tune quantile choices and merge thresholds. (Spike: ENG-100322)
2) Runtime integration: add per-route online estimator and tranche metadata to the request router; extend packer to use tranche-aware slotting.
3) Kernel hints: expose kernel hint API on tranche metadata and add runtime mapping table for kernel selection.
4) Canary rollout: instrument metrics and roll out to low-traffic routes for 48h soak, then to medium routes with gradual traffic ramp.
5) Full rollout: monitor error budgets and cost metrics for two weeks before promoting to default.

Observability & testing:
- New metrics: tranche_count, average_tranche_variance, padded_tokens_saved, tranche_kernel_mismatch_rate, tranche_recompute_rate.
- Dashboards: per-route pad-savings heatmap and kernel-affinity mismatch alert.
- Tests: unit tests for t-digest estimator, integration test for packer behavior with synthetic traces, load test with replayed customer traffic, A/B compare vs baseline.

Rollout & migration notes:
- Provide route-level knobs: {enable_trancheer, quantile_spec, max_coalescing_ms, kernel_affinity_preference}.
- For Dedicated customers with strict isolation, default to disabled; add an opt-in flag and an operator safety check for memory/pinned-GPU constraints.

Dependencies: requires new runtime API for kernel hints (runtime-1.20), lightweight t-digest library (internal), and console dashboard plumbing for new metrics.

Open questions:
- Best default quantile grid for general workloads? (experiment candidates: [p10,p30,p60,p85,p95] vs [p20,p40,p70,p90])
- How aggressive should tranche merging be for tail-heavy routes?
